summary: order-service p99 >5s and ledger-db statement timeouts are collateral damage from a shared-database CPU saturation caused by portfolio-service deployment dep-5905 (v4.5.0, 2026-05-05T08:56). The release added a new holdings P&L query — "SELECT * FROM trades WHERE account_id=$1 AND executed_at > $2" — that runs as a full Seq Scan on the 48M-row trades table (no supporting index; the deploy notes "no migration included"). These slow full-table scans drove ledger-db CPU from ~30% to ~96% and active connections from ~62 to ~190, saturating the shared Postgres instance. order-service (no release this week, flat CPU/memory) then began timing out on its own writes ("canceling statement due to statement timeout (INSERT INTO orders)"). The DBA autovacuum change (cfg-2903, 08:00) is a red herring: it preceded onset by ~56 minutes and disk usage stayed flat (~71%).

ranked_hypotheses.title: portfolio-service deploy dep-5905 added an unindexed trades query that saturated shared ledger-db
ranked_hypotheses.statement: portfolio-service v4.5.0 (dep-5905, 08:56) introduced a new holdings P&L query 'SELECT * FROM trades WHERE account_id=$1 AND executed_at > $2' with no supporting index ('no migration included'). Under normal request rate it executes as a Seq Scan over the 48M-row trades table, driving ledger-db CPU to ~96%, active connections from ~62 to ~190 and slow queries from ~1/min to ~140/min. The shared ledger-db becomes the bottleneck, so order-service's own writes (INSERT INTO orders) queue and hit statement timeouts, producing p99 >5s and 5xx. order-service is only where the symptom was noticed.

causal_chain.claim: dep-5905 deploys portfolio-service v4.5.0 at 08:56 with a new trades query and no index migration
New query runs as Seq Scan on 48M-row trades table in ledger-db, attributed application_name=portfolio-service
ledger-db CPU 30%->96%, connections ~62->~190, slow queries ~1->~140/min from the 08:50 bucket
Shared ledger-db saturation delays order-service INSERTs -> statement timeouts, p99 >5s (order-service CPU/memory flat, no release)

assumptions: The new query has no index on (account_id, executed_at) so Postgres chooses a seq scan
order-service and portfolio-service share the same physical ledger-db instance
Baseline attestations of ~150ms order-service p99 reflect pre-incident SLO

ranked_hypotheses.title: DBA autovacuum config change on ledger-db caused the saturation
ranked_hypotheses.statement: cfg-2903 changed ledger-db autovacuum_vacuum_scale_factor from 0.2 to 0.1 at 08:00; more aggressive autovacuum could consume CPU/IO and bloat the planner statistics, slowing queries on ledger-db including order-service INSERTs.

causal_chain.claim: ledger-db CPU saturation at 08:50 (56 min later, uncorrelated)

ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Precedes onset by ~56 minutes with no change for 50+ min, while onset aligns to the minute with the deploy. Disk usage stayed flat (~71%) so no bloat/disk symptom. The dominant slow query is explicitly a per-request SELECT from portfolio-service, not an autovacuum-induced effect.

ranked_hypotheses.title: order-service resource exhaustion (pool/CPU/memory)
ranked_hypotheses.statement: order-service's own resources (db connection pool, CPU, memory) exhausted, causing its INSERTs to time out.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: order-service CPU flat ~40% and memory flat ~60%; no deploy or config change on order-service. Its db_pool_in_use rose (13->46) only in response to slow ledger-db, and the timeout is on the server side ('canceling statement due to statement timeout'), consistent with downstream DB saturation, not local exhaustion.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Load-driven capacity saturation on the shared database
ranked_hypotheses.statement: Incoming traffic grew beyond provisioned ledger-db capacity, saturating CPU/connections.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: request_rate into portfolio-service and order-service was flat across onset (~570 req/s and unchanged), and there was a discrete deployment change rather than a gradual load ramp.

facts.statement: order-service p99 latency broke from ~150ms to 694ms (max 5608ms) in the 08:50 bucket and stayed ~5.2s.
order-service logged 284 'canceling statement due to statement timeout (INSERT INTO orders)' errors starting 09:00:42.
portfolio-service p99 latency broke in the same 08:50 bucket (avg 1539ms, max 7057ms) and stayed ~7000ms.
ledger-db CPU rose from ~30% to ~96% beginning in the 08:50 bucket.
ledger-db active connections rose from ~62 to ~190-200 beginning in the 08:50 bucket.
ledger-db slow_queries_per_min rose from ~1 to ~140 beginning in the 08:50 bucket.
ledger-db slow queries are 'SELECT * FROM trades WHERE account_id=$1 AND executed_at > $2' executed as Seq Scan on 48,211,907 rows, application_name=portfolio-service.
The only deployment in the window is dep-5905 portfolio-service v4.5.0 at 08:56, whose changes are a new trades query with no migration, not rolled back.
portfolio-service logged 'deployment dep-5905 (v4.5.0) rollout complete' at 08:56:32 and first slow holdings P&L query (7459ms) at 08:59:39.
order-service had zero deployments in the window.
The only config change is cfg-2903 (ledger-db autovacuum_vacuum_scale_factor 0.2->0.1) at 08:00.
ledger-db disk_used_pct stayed flat near 71% throughout.
order-service CPU (~40%) and memory (~60%) stayed flat throughout.
portfolio-service request_rate stayed flat ~570 req/s across onset.
order-service and portfolio-service both depend on the shared ledger-db.

assumptions: order-service and portfolio-service share the same physical ledger-db instance (both have db edges to the shared ledger-db node).
The new dep-5905 query has no index on (account_id, executed_at), so Postgres chooses a 48M-row Seq Scan.
Pre-incident p99 of ~150ms (order-service) and ~180ms (portfolio-service) are the normal baselines.
The 'new query on trades filtered by account_id + executed_at' in dep-5905 corresponds to the logged 'SELECT * FROM trades WHERE account_id=$1 AND executed_at > $2' slow query.

timeline.event: DBA config change cfg-2903 applied to ledger-db (autovacuum_vacuum_scale_factor 0.2->0.1). No symptom follows for ~50 min.
Onset bucket: order-service p99 150ms->694ms, portfolio-service p99 ->1539ms, ledger-db CPU ->96%, connections ->200, slow queries ->140/min.
Deployment dep-5905 portfolio-service v4.5.0 goes live (new trades query, no index migration).
portfolio-service logs 'deployment dep-5905 (v4.5.0) rollout complete, all pods ready'.
First ledger-db slow query (8690ms, Seq Scan on trades, application_name=portfolio-service).
portfolio-service first 'holdings P&L query took 7459ms' warning.
order-service first 'canceling statement due to statement timeout (INSERT INTO orders)' error.
Latest data: services still degraded; dep-5905 still live, not rolled back.

recommended_actions.action: Roll back portfolio-service deployment dep-5905 (v4.5.0) to the prior version to remove the unindexed trades query immediately.
recommended_actions.rationale: Only change coincident with onset; removing it should stop the Seq Scans and relieve shared ledger-db CPU.

recommended_actions.action: Add a supporting index on trades(account_id, executed_at) (CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY) and re-check the query plan before re-releasing the feature.
recommended_actions.rationale: The new query scans the 48M-row trades table; an index lets the plan avoid full scans.

recommended_actions.action: Add per-application workloads / statement_timeout guardrails and query-plan checks for shared ledger-db so one service cannot saturate the shared instance.
recommended_actions.rationale: A single service's unindexed query starved order-service writes on the shared DB.

recommended_actions.action: Do not revert cfg-2903 on the basis of this incident; keep autovacuum change but verify with DBA that it played no role.
recommended_actions.rationale: Autovacuum change preceded onset by ~56 min and disk stayed flat, so it is not the cause.

recommended_actions.action: Add a deployment-level gate that flags new queries with no accompanying migration/index for shared DBs, and alert on ledger-db CPU/connections/slow-query rate.
recommended_actions.rationale: Prevent recurrence of unindexed-query-on-shared-DB class of failures.

data_gaps: Historical-incident search backend returned 503 (tc-019), so no comparison to past similar incidents was possible.
A ledger-db slow_queries_per_min re-query around 08:36-09:10 failed with 503 (tc-025); finer-grained onset timing of slow queries is unavailable beyond the 08:50 bucket and the first log at 08:58:38.
No visibility into the trades table's index definitions or query plan history to confirm the migration/index gap directly.
No direct telemetry that order-service and portfolio-service share the same ledger-db instance vs separate schemas; inferred from the shared-node dependency graph.
Postgres logs for ledger-db only show WARN-level slow queries; no autovacuum/IO metrics to fully quantify autovacuum impact (disk metric only).
